note: Processing is a CHAIN, not always a single step - some ingredients cook directly into food (beef -> grill -> grilled beef), others need an intermediate processing item first (wheat -> mill -> flour -> bake -> bread). next_item_id just points to whatever comes next in the chain, one link at a time; follow it repeatedly (it may point to another ingredients item, or to the final food item) rather than assuming every ingredient is one step from food.
title: Ingredients

processing_method.note: grill, bake, cook, mill, or none (eaten/used raw, or not directly edible/usable at all - e.g. cotton before being processed into cloth).

next_item_id.note: the item this becomes after processing_method is applied. May be another ingredients item that still needs further processing (e.g. wheat -> ingredient_flour, which doesn't exist yet - a real content gap) or the final food_* item (or ingredient_*_grilled, which lives in the food category despite the prefix). '' if processing_method is none, OR if processing_method is set but the resulting item hasn't been created yet (also a real gap, not an error - e.g. corn/sunflower/egg have no next item yet).
